missions.title: The friendly introduction
paragraphs: Nora, Sami, Leila and Omar meet to write a short radio script for their neighbourhood. Sami writes a welcome for a short café story. Nora checks that a listener would know who is speaking. The opening gives enough context without becoming a long explanation.

A radio scene has to guide the listener without a picture. A clear introduction can explain the setting, while a carefully chosen sound makes it easier to imagine. The friends write their own short material and do not copy song lyrics. Their programme stays gentle, friendly and easy to follow.
The important result is not a perfect performance. It is a clearer shared experience. Each person can describe one detail, give a reason for noticing it, and listen to another point of view.

In a conversation about this subject, you could say: “You're listening to our little neighbourhood show.” “Over to you for today's cheerful book note.” “Thanks for tuning in. We hope you enjoyed the café story.”

paragraphs: A handover document includes last month's procedure. The procedure changed earlier this week. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.
